slides.0.title: Level 2 Assessment
slides.0.subtitle: Northern/southern crus, grapes and rules
slides.1.title: Level 2 recap
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Tiers and proportions
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Côtes du Rhône: Grenache ≥30% and Syrah + Mourvèdre ≥20% (from the 2022 harvest); Villages: Grenache ≥40% and Syrah + Mourvèdre ≥25%; 21 named villages; proportions measured on estate plantings
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Northern Rhône
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Côte-Rôtie (1940; Syrah ≥80%, Viognier ≤20%); Condrieu (100% Viognier); Château-Grillet (single estate, about 4 ha); Hermitage (vin de paille dried ≥45 days); Crozes-Hermitage (largest); Saint-Joseph (1956, right bank); Cornas (100% Syrah, 1938); Saint-Péray (Marsanne/Roussanne, still and sparkling)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Southern Rhône
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Châteauneuf-du-Pape (1936; 13 varieties / 18 entries; hand harvest and sorting; left bank); Gigondas 1971, Vacqueyras 1990, Beaumes-de-Venise 2005, Vinsobres 2006, Rasteau dry red 2010, Cairanne 2016, Laudun 2024; Lirac 1947, Tavel 1936 (right bank)
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Other names
slides.1.highlights.3.content: VDN: fortifying spirit at 5–10% of the must (Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise, Rasteau VDN); Clairette de Die ancestrale is mainly Muscat with a single fermentation finished in bottle; Ventoux, Luberon, Grignan-les-Adhémar and others are not among the 18 crus
slides.1.content: Pass the assessment to move on to Level 3: Diploma/MW refinement.
slides.2.componentProps.slide.title: 📋 Level 2 Final Assessment
For red Côtes du Rhône, what are the minimum Grenache and Syrah + Mourvèdre shares (vines in production, from the 2022 harvest)?
Côtes du Rhône: Grenache ≥30% and Syrah + Mourvèdre ≥20%; 40%/25% is Villages.
How many villages may add their name to Côtes du Rhône Villages?
What are the Syrah minimum and the Viognier ceiling in Côte-Rôtie?
Syrah ≥80%; Viognier at most 20% of the vines in Syrah plots, often co-fermented with Syrah.
Which appellation makes red wine from Syrah alone?
Cornas uses Syrah only; Côte-Rôtie may include Viognier, and Hermitage and Saint-Joseph a little Marsanne/Roussanne.
For Hermitage vin de paille, how long must the grapes dry at minimum?
At least 45 days, exceeding 350 g/L sugar at pressing.
What are Saint-Péray's wines and grapes?
A. White (still and sparkling); Marsanne and Roussanne
Saint-Péray is white only, from Marsanne and Roussanne.
Which is NOT a permitted Châteauneuf-du-Pape variety?
Marsanne is not on the list; Counoise, Muscardin and Cinsault are permitted.
In which year was the Gigondas decree issued?
Which appellation did the INAO national committee approve in September 2024 as the 18th cru?
In a VDN such as Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise, how much neutral spirit is added, as a share of the must volume?
5% to 10% (at least 96% vol.), halting fermentation and keeping natural sugar.
